# Production readiness

What stands between swiftdc and a decompiler whose output can be trusted without
hand-checking it. Organised by **risk**, not by feature appeal.

Each item is `[status] claim — evidence`. Status is one of **OPEN**, **FIXED**,
**MITIGATED**, **UNKNOWN**, **DEAD END** (measured, did not beat baseline) or
**SUPERSEDED** (an intermediate status a later entry replaces). *UNKNOWN means nobody has measured it* — it is not
a synonym for "probably fine", and an UNKNOWN in Soundness or Completeness
outranks an OPEN in Reconstruction quality.

Every claim here should carry either a commit, a file:line, or a command you can
re-run. Claims without one are marked UNKNOWN by definition.

Last comprehensive audit: 2026-11-10, against 9369b0e. Every OPEN and UNKNOWN
entry (93) was checked against the code and, where a fixture or a small build could show
it, reproduced with a release binary. 11 were fixed or superseded and are
marked so, 7 frame-memory entries are SUPERSEDED by one, and about 20 had
stale counts, renamed symbols or a wrong stated cause, now corrected and marked
"audited 2026-11-10". Entries not re-measured (they need a private app or a
whole large image) say so. A 1,210-line block the 2026-11-08 commit 077d4f0
pasted a second time, with one entry in the earlier copy corrupted, was
removed, keeping the later copy. At that date, two remaining OPEN entries
rendered a wrong value or crashed: the async-context assumption (`incomingLeaf`)
and the nested ObjC type encoding. Later hash-pinned entries below record
targeted follow-ups; they do not constitute another sweep of all 93 entries.

Previously audited: 2026-10-12, unified merge of all feature branches (MachOSwiftSection
0.22.0, Capstone 6, x8 indirect returns, arm64e preflight, async funclets), then a
sweep of every subcommand over 7 large apps and 5 dyld-cache frameworks (partial
when written: Prime Video, Fiery Feeds, part of Swiftcord). Re-audited the same
day against HEAD by an agent that read this file, `handoff.md` and the research
docs against the source; its stale-claim findings are corrected below.

The 2026-10-12 semantic follow-up (`0ace2da`…`4140b8c`) ends at **485
passing tests with fixture presence enforced**, including 217,728 native CCMP
comparisons and 486 native CSETM executions. Each fix's test was seen red with
that fix disabled. This is measured regression coverage of the reductions; no
overall decompilation-accuracy percentage is claimed.

The 2026-10-12 validation follow-up adds native Swift scoring and replaces
all repository Python scripts. Scoring separates agreement from coverage,
rejects duplicate analyses and ambiguous exits, and checks an optional image
UUID before reporting. The width fixture's 1,174 cases and seven independent
Swift integer-return samples all agree in live/trace checks. This is an integer
sample corpus, not an app-wide accuracy estimate. Commands and public defaults
are in [INSTRUMENTATION.md](INSTRUMENTATION.md).
Verification: `SWIFTDC_REQUIRE_FIXTURES=1 swift test` passes 530 tests in 11
suites. Signedness and duplicate-analysis scoring tests were each seen failing
under an isolated mutation, then rebuilt and passed after restoration. CLI
tests cover verified/refuted/incomplete/invalid-data exits and explicit
incomplete allowance. The Swift tooling smoke checks cover 21 fuzz subcommand
runs, the quick benchmark matrix, and identical regenerated fixture assembly
apart from its generator header.

The fuzz harness is now `swift Tools/fuzz.swift container|metadata ...`; its
`splitmix64-swift/1` sequence differs from the historical harness referenced
below. Historical seed/mutant counts remain historical evidence. The new
harness reports timeouts separately from crashes and counts subcommand runs.
The Swift benchmark checks every repeat's output and exit status. Its smoke
results do not replace previously recorded release performance measurements.


## 2026-11-24: the result of a typed-throwing call ends at its error edge

**FIXED (soundness).** After a call to a synchronous `throws(E)` callee
that has a result, x0 stayed bound as that result on the caller's error
path, where it holds the thrown error or nothing defined. Reproduced on
compiled Swift three times: in typedcatch.swift, and independently in
two functions of a native fixture family written to test error handling.

| Function | Rendered | True |
|---|---|---|
| `caughtKind` (-O): `do { return try hold(grade(n)) } catch { return tally(error) }` | `return TypedCatch.tally(r0)`, r0 being `grade`'s result | the argument is the thrown `Kind` |
| the same at -Onone | `TypedCatch.tally((r0 & 0xffffffff))` | the same |
| a rethrow that boxes the caught payload (-Onone) | `Boxed.__allocating_init(code:)((r0 + 677))` | the error's payload plus 677 |
| a catch reading a thrown class's field (-Osize) | `OUTLINED_FUNCTION_42(r0)` on the `x21 != 0` edge | x0 is the thrown object |

The tracer now gives a block an error edge when it ends in `cbz` or
`cbnz` on 64-bit x21, its last call prints `throws(E)`, the call is not
proven non-throwing, and nothing writes x21 after it. Along that edge
every register and frame slot whose value is, or is computed from, the
call's x0 result is forgotten. Nothing is named as the error. The
success edge is unchanged, and so is untyped `throws`, whose error is in
x21.

**OPEN, left as today's behaviour:** a value loaded through the result
pointer, a word of an indirect result, and the second register of a
two-register result are not forgotten on the error edge (the drafted
arms for them had no test that killed them and were cut); an x21 test
made in a later block than the call, or by `cmp` and `b.cond`, is not
recognised as the error edge.

Blast radius against 964f0d6: 8 structured lines in 4 files.
libTypedCatch at -Onone and -O, 2 each: the two rows above.
typed-error-inactive-O-oracle and -Osize-oracle, 2 each: one stored byte
on an error path changes from `(? & 255)` to the raw `w23`, one unknown
spelled as another. The four toolchain dylibs are unchanged. Cost:
instructions +0.17%, footprint +0.24%.

Verified: TypedCatchErrorEdgeTests (bodies from instruction words for
each premise, and the fixture through the whole image and a filter) and
the emulator sweep with both libTypedCatch images. Nine mutations seen
red: the refinement itself, typed only, not proven non-throwing, x21
unwritten since the call, the tested register, its width, the edge's
polarity, the existential error counted as typed, and values computed
from the result. Full enforcing suite: 2,220 tests.

## 2026-11-24: a typed error is named from x0 only beside a proven direct result

**FIXED (soundness), sprint 15, E03-a.** A typed error's case was named
from x0 at a throw exit unless one veto fired (a result of five
`UInt64`s). A typed error is in x0 only when the function's result is
direct too; beside an indirect result it goes through a buffer and x0 is
whatever was left there. Reproduced at -Onone, -O and -Osize
(errorcarrier.swift with two authored bodies in errorcarrier.s):

| Function | Truth | Rendered |
|---|---|---|
| `wide(Int) throws(Fault) -> Quint` | stores `.high` through the error buffer, x0 = 1 | `throw ErrorCarrier.Fault.mid` |
| `opaque<A>(A, Int) throws(Fault) -> A` | the same | `throw ErrorCarrier.Fault.mid` |

In the `wide` render the store of the real tag, `mem8[x1] = 2`, was the
line above the wrong `throw`.

The case is now named only when a direct carrier is proven
(`provesDirectTypedErrorCarrier`): a synchronous function named by its
own symbol with a plain declaration head, an error that is a
non-resilient enum with no payload, and a result proven direct: a
direct scalar, a complete struct within four registers, or a tuple of
one-register scalars within four, labels allowed. Everything else
renders `throw ?`. The five-word veto and its test are unchanged.

Cost in true renders, measured: none on the fixtures. Across 26 built
typed-throw and throwing images the tip printed 17 named-case throws
(`typedScale` in five Reconstruction builds, `probeDirect` and
`probeFour` six each); the gate keeps all 17. Declined by the gate and
without a fixture behind them: async typed throwers (today's tip names
none), results such as `(String, Int)` or an Optional of a struct,
specialized or metadata-recovered names, and single-case error enums.
The five apps were not measured.

Blast radius against 088cfd9: 12 structured lines, all in the three
libErrorCarrier images (the two wrong throws at each level). Cost:
instructions +0.04%, footprint +0.30%.

Verified: TypedErrorCarrierTests (three image tests over the direct
controls, the two indirect throwers, the compiler's own indirect thrower
and an async one; one unit test that removes a premise at a time) and
the emulator sweep with libErrorCarrier.O. Twelve mutations seen red,
one per premise: the use-site proof, the direct result, async, the
error's tag, resilience, the declaration head, the function's own
symbol, a generic parameter in the result, the four-register struct
budget, the tuple budget, a tuple element's width, and a tuple label.
Full enforcing suite: 2,212 tests.

## 2026-11-24: a register stored and never reloaded is clobbered for every caller up the chain

**FIXED (soundness), sprint 20, M01-a.** The card's own case was already
guarded: a direct `bl` to a body that leaves x19 changed makes x19
unknown from the body's evidence. The hole was one call further away. The
set of clobbers a summary carries to its callers dropped every register
the body stores anywhere, including one it stores, overwrites and never
loads back. A caller two calls up then read the register as preserved.
Reproduced with authored assembly (spill_carry.s), run natively:

| Function | Rendered | Machine |
|---|---|---|
| `SpillCarry.relayed`, `tailed`, `parked` | `return arg0` | arg1 (2 for the vector 1, 2) |
| `SpillCarry.fixed` | `return 7` | 11 |

A stored register now stays out of the carried clobbers only if the body
has a load into it, or a callee's effect clobbers it. Otherwise it
carries like one never stored. Four controls keep `return arg0`: a body
that saves and reloads, one that reloads through a helper, one that hands
the register to a callee that restores it, and one whose callee restores
it.

A fourth rule in the drafted change, counting a callee's proven reload,
was removed: deleting it changed no test and no render.

Blast radius against e4c9b94: 8 structured lines, all in libSpillCarry
(the four false returns). No other fixture and none of the four
toolchain dylibs changes. Cost: instructions +0.08%, footprint -0.30%.
The concern that async funclets replacing x22 would add summary rebuilds
did not show: the two large inputs are flat.

One existing expectation flips, in
`strictBodyReturnProofsFollowFrameAliasesThroughAllActualCallInputsIfPresent`:
the alias leaves there store x19 and never reload it, so they now carry
the clobber.

Verified: SpillCarryTests (native results through dlopen, the renders in
the array, filtered and streaming views, and the summaries), and the
emulator sweep with libSpillCarry. Three mutations seen red: the carry
itself (34 issues), a body's own reload (9), a callee's clobber (5). Full
enforcing suite: 2,208 tests.

## 2026-11-23: a stack argument past a hole, or past the sixteenth word

**FIXED (soundness), sprint 16, M04-a.** When a call may take stack
arguments, the tracer walks the words above sp to see which frame
addresses the callee is handed. The walk stopped at the first word with
no recorded store and after 16 words. An address after a padding word, or
in the seventeenth word, was never handed over, and the local it points
at kept its value across the call. Reproduced with authored assembly
(stackhole.s); the sinks store 11 through the pointer they are passed:

| Function | Rendered | Machine |
|---|---|---|
| `StackHole.padded()`: a word at sp, an 8-byte hole, then `&local` | `return 7` | 11 |
| `StackHole.seventeenth()`: `&local` in the seventeenth word | `return 7` | 11 |

The analysis showed the cut: `call sp+0=1` for `padded`, and exactly
sixteen words for `seventeenth`. A hole is real in compiled code: an
8-byte argument followed by a 16-byte-aligned one leaves one.

The arguments are now every frame word stored since the last call, from
sp up to the prologue's register save area, provided a word is stored at
sp itself. The first stack argument is at sp, so with nothing there a
frame address kept in a slot further up is a local of this frame. Without
that condition three `-Onone` functions lost a true `return r0`, because
a spilled frame address counted as an argument; an existing test
(`onlyAFramePointerLostAtAMustJoinEscapes`) pins the case and caught it.

Blast radius against c2217e8: 8 structured lines in 2 files. libStackHole,
4: the two false returns. libIndirectResultOrder, 4: `_alias_result_make`
at -Onone stores a word at sp and a frame address above it before calling
`Packet.init`, whose stack arity is not proven, so `let r0 = …; return r0`
becomes the call and `memcpy(&result, local_48, 40)`. A decline of a true
render: proving the callee's stack arity from its signature would keep
it. The four toolchain dylibs are unchanged. Cost: instructions +0.05%.

Verified: StackHoleTests (four bodies from instruction words and the
fixture through the pipeline and the bare tracer) and the emulator sweep,
which now holds libStackHole. Six mutations seen red: the hole, the
16-word cap, the save-area bound, words above the first, the
no-stack-argument callee, and the first-word condition (which also turns
the existing test red). Full enforcing suite: 2,204 tests.

## 2026-11-23: a callee whose result is Never hands back no value

**FIXED (soundness), sprint 14, E07-a.** A call to a function whose
signature result is `Never` was given a result like any other call. Such
a callee comes back only by throwing, and x0 on that path is what it left
or a typed error's payload. Reproduced on compiled Swift at -Onone, -O
and -Osize (nosuccess.swift) and on authored assembly (no_success.s):

| Function | Rendered | True |
|---|---|---|
| `relay(Int) throws -> Int`, ending `bl stop; ret` | `return try stop((arg0 + 1))` | throws what `stop` threw |
| `haltCode(Int) -> Int`, a catch reading the typed error | `return (halt(arg0) + 1)` | the error's payload plus one |

The tracer's call transfer now leaves x0 unknown after a callee whose
own printed signature has the result `Swift.Never` (`CallFacts.
returnsNeverByName`). The call stays, as a statement, followed by the
unresolved exit or `return ?`. A `throws(Never) -> Int` callee keeps its
Int: the `Never` there is the thrown type. A callee with no signature
keeps its result.

The card asked for the control-flow edge after the call to be cut. It is
not: the compiler marks only C callees `noreturn`, so after a
`throws -> Never` call the next instruction is the error path, and
cutting the edge would delete the catch. The -O `caught` fixture shows
the catch running straight after the call.

Blast radius against 004f0ed: 19 lines in the structured view, all in
the four new images and all of the two shapes above; 0 lines in every
other fixture and in the four toolchain dylibs. Cost: instructions
+0.20%, footprint +0.15%.

**OPEN, found on the way** and drafted as its own patch: after any
synchronous `throws(E)` callee that has a result, x0 on the error path
is still named as that result (`tally(r0)` in a catch).

Verified: NoSuccessResultTests, seen red under four mutations: the gate
off (18 issues, on the compiled and the authored callers), `Never`
matched anywhere in the name (5), any thrower taken to have no result
(6), x0 left as the call's result (18). A write clearing v0 as well was
removed: a `-> Double` caller showed it changes nothing. Full enforcing
suite: 2,197 tests.

## 2026-11-23: a float between two integers keeps them in separate registers

**FIXED (soundness), sprint 17, L03-a, latent.** `SwiftLowering` counted a
struct argument's general registers as the set of 8-byte chunks its
integer scalars fall in, so `{ Int16, Float16, Int16 }` counted one. The
Swift calling convention merges only neighbouring integer entries and
never across a float (clang `SwiftCallingConv.cpp` at the 6.4.2 pin; the
audit's IR shows `(i16, half, i16)`), so the struct takes two general
registers and one vector register, and every formal after it would be
placed one register early.

Nothing renders wrongly today, and the fix changes no render: the layout
reader has no size for `Float16`, so a struct holding one has an untrusted
layout and no count (`swiftdc layout` prints `typeDescriptorNotFound
(qualifiedTypeName: "Swift.Float16")`), and every function of
fpbarrierpieces.swift renders `return ?`. A 2-byte float is the only way
to put a float between two integers of one chunk, so `Float16` is the
only way in. The count is fixed first so that teaching the reader
`Float16`, which is now listed as a completeness item, cannot open the
defect.

Scalars are now collected as ordered pieces with their bytes. An integer
starts a new register unless the piece just before it is an integer
ending in the same chunk; overlapping pieces decline; the four-register
limit runs on the merged count.

Blast radius against 1df4124: 0 lines in all four views over 3,284
renders. Cost: instructions -0.07%, footprint +0.15%.

Verified: FPBarrierPieceTests. Four tests on hand-built layouts, seen red
under nine mutations (the barrier, merging at all, the chunk test, the
overlap decline, the String and Optional pieces and their guards, the
four-register limit). Two image tests pin the decline at -O and -Onone:
no count for any of the four structs, and no formal named after one. They
were not seen red; they go red when the reader learns `Float16`, and are
then replaced by the placement the fixture states. Full enforcing suite:
2,191 tests.

## 2026-11-23: nested Optional results are held to the compiler's x8 use

**GUARDED (tests), sprint 18, L06-a.** The card suspected that an
Optional result is called direct with no bound on nesting or tag growth:
`SwiftLowering.of` recurses on the payload's `isDirect`, so a callee with
no body could be denied its x8 buffer. It does not reproduce. An Optional
needs a fifth piece only around four pieces with no spare bit pattern,
and no payload the lowering admits has that shape. A struct of four words
is already unknown to it, so `Four?` never had a claim to withdraw.

optionalnesting.swift holds one maker per admitted payload family, nested
two levels (three for UInt64), beside `Four?` and an Optional pair of
buffer pointers, which do return through x8. The compiled bodies are the
oracle, at -O and -Onone: a result type called direct never has a maker
that reads its incoming x8, 17 nested makers keep their claim, and the
two that cross the boundary have none and read x8. At -O the linker
folds `makeMetatype` and `makeUnmanaged` onto accessors with the same
code, so those two are checked at -Onone only.

**OPEN, found on the way:** `SwiftLowering` calls any type ending in
`.Type` direct. An existential metatype of four or more witness-bearing
protocols is five words and returns through x8. It is listed in
ABI-SPRINTS.md under the drafted sprints.

Verified: OptionalNestingLoweringTests, seen red under three mutations of
the claim it guards: declining a nested Optional (71 issues), calling an
unlisted type direct (17), and taking a tuple for a function type (7).
No Core change, so no render change.

## 2026-11-23: a callee that writes above its entry sp

**FIXED (soundness).** A caller's frame slot was taken to survive any call
that was passed no address of it. A callee that stores above the sp it was
entered with writes that frame anyway. The emulator sweep found two
renders this made false, and the new fixture a third:

| Function | Rendered | Machine |
|---|---|---|
| `_entry_pointer_copy_probe` (libCallerFrameAlias, three levels) | `if (1)` | branch not taken |
| `_async_memory_st4` (libAsyncMemoryEffects) | `return // x0 = 7` | 0x4444444444444444 |
| `_frame_reach_through_probe` and three more (libFrameReach) | `return // x0 = 3` | 99 |

`CallerFrameReach` scans each body once, following the depth of sp below
its entry value as a lower bound over the body's own branches, and
records three things in the function's summary:

- the bytes above the entry sp it may store to, directly or through an
  address it made from sp or x29. The caller forgets its `[sp, sp + n)`
  at the call. Compiled code does this to its stack arguments;
- the offsets above the entry sp it makes an address of. The caller's
  slot there escapes, as one whose address was passed. Machine-outlined
  code does this, running on its caller's sp;
- the depth of sp at each direct call. The closure takes a callee's reach
  less that depth, so a reach that stays inside the calling body's own
  frame stops there.

A store nothing bounds (sp indexed by a register, sp from a register
with no frame record) forgets the caller's whole frame. An address loaded
back from memory, indexed by a register or handed to a call is not
followed: what a callee writes through a pointer to a local is taken to
stay inside the local.

The first version was a yes/no fact that forgot the whole frame. Its
blast radius showed why that is wrong: one outlined value function in
each of libSwiftOperators and libSwiftCompilerPluginMessageHandling
stores to its stack arguments, and every caller lost real renders
(`&result` became `x8`, a named witness call became an indirect call).
With bytes and points, the four toolchain dylibs render unchanged.

Blast radius against c639424 (`Tools/blast-radius.sh --real --perf`,
structured view, 10 files, 1,367 lines):

- libCallerFrameAlias, 8 lines at each level: the `if (1)`, and the slot
  above it, in `_entry_pointer_copy_probe`; one `if (0)` in each of two
  oracles whose callee stores 72 bytes above its entry sp, over the slot
  the condition reads.
- libAsyncMemoryEffects, 1 line: the `x0 = 7`.
- libFrameReach, 4 lines: the false `x0 = 3` renders.
- narrow-integer-return-SwiftArgumentBoundary.Osize-oracle, 2 lines:
  `type metadata for …` becomes `?` in one `swift_allocObject` call. An
  outlined fragment takes the address of a slot of `_main` and returns it
  in x20; the slot above it now escapes. A decline of a true render.
- The two Go programs and their stripped copies, 374 and 294 lines each:
  Go passes arguments and results in the caller's frame, so its callees
  store above their entry sp. Go is not a target.

Cost: instructions +0.86% in total (9,099G to 9,178G over 3,268 renders),
footprint +0.27%, within budget. `CalleeRegisterSummary` grows 24 bytes
(144 to 168).

Not measured: the five apps. `-Osize` apps use the machine outliner
heavily, and an outlined fragment that takes a caller slot's address now
escapes that slot at the call.

Verified: CallerFrameReachTests (20 synthetic bodies with their bytes
and points, the closure over hand-built summaries, the call depths, and
the fixtures through the whole image, a filter, the streamed image and
one function at a time) and the emulator sweep, now with libFrameReach
and no known false statement. 34 mutations, one per rule in the scan,
the closure, the three summary copies, the plumbing, the three closure
call sites and the three tracer effects, each seen red. Full enforcing
suite: 2,181 tests.

## 2026-11-23: an emulator checks what the pipeline states

**ADDED (validation).** `Fixtures/Sample/emuoracle.c` builds `emu-oracle` on Unicorn 2.1.4. It maps
a thin arm64 Mach-O, starts at any address with any registers, and reports
how the run ended (returned, trapped, hung, faulted, left the image), the
final registers, every conditional branch with whether it was taken, and
every call. The native oracle can only call exported functions with a C
convention. This one runs a stripped body, a funclet or a fragment.

EmulatorOracleTests sweeps 18 fixture images. For each function it seeds
the registers from the `analysis.entry` record, runs 8 input vectors twice
(unseeded registers all distinct, then all zero), and checks three kinds of
statement against the machine: a `render.return-value` claim in x0, the x0
a `return // x0 = …` comment names, and a branch condition rendered `1` or
`0`. A claim that depends on a stack argument is skipped, because a run
seeds no stack. A run that calls out of the image checks nothing after the
call. The default list checks 1,868 returns and 216 constant conditions in
7 s. `SWIFTDC_EMU_IMAGES=all` swept all 671 fixture dylibs: 12,854
functions, 205,664 runs, 89,776 returns and 4,744 conditions.

It found two false statements no test had caught. Both were listed in
`knownFalseStatements` and are **FIXED** by the entry above; the list is
empty again.

- **FIXED** `_async_memory_st4` (libAsyncMemoryEffects.dylib) renders
  `return // x0 = 7`. The fragment it calls writes 64 bytes with `st4`
  across the caller's frame, and the machine returns
  0x4444444444444444. The existing test asserted only the native value.
- **FIXED** `_entry_pointer_copy_probe` (libCallerFrameAlias, -Onone, -O
  and -Osize) renders `if (1)` for a compare of a frame slot with 99. The
  callee writes 99 to that slot through a pointer made from its entry
  stack pointer, so the machine does not take the branch.

The emulator agrees with native execution on 11 cases from the sprint
fixtures, including a trap, a loop and the swifterror register.

Unicorn is now a build requirement of the enforcing suite, like Go:
`Tools/ci/environment.sh` fails without it, hosted CI installs it, and
the fixture cache key includes its version.

Verified: each check was seen red. Dropping the zero baseline, the
`x0 =` check or the constant-condition check makes a known false
statement stop disagreeing. Dropping the stack-argument skip reports
`sub_790` and `sub_32d0`. Swapping add and subtract in the tracer
reports 36 return claims in libSwiftArgumentBoundary.O.dylib, and none
with the return check removed.

## 2026-11-23: the sprint fixtures run natively

**ADDED (tests).** Each sprint fixture says in a comment what its code
does, and five are hand-written assembly. Nothing ran them: a test
compared swiftdc's render with a reading of the source.
`Fixtures/Sample/sprintnative.c` builds `sprint-native-oracle`, which
loads ten fixture images and prints what each call did: returned and with
what, threw, trapped, or hung. A throwing Swift function is called
through a trampoline that clears x21 and hands it back; a call that may
not return runs in a child process under a one-second alarm.

It makes 39 observations, and all agree with the comments: the error
lookalikes return 5, 7 and 6 with no error; the arm without the throw
hook returns 7 for a zero argument and throws for a non-zero one; the
trap-tail wrappers trap on 0 and hang on 9, with and without symbols; two
reads of one field differ by 18 across the access twin; the deferred
store reaches 99 on the throwing path; the late-installed method, sent as
a message with 5 and 9, returns 5.

The first run found one defect in a fixture: `always` in `hookpath.s`
used x19 without saving it, and the caller's x19 was gone. It is fixed,
and its render is unchanged.

SprintNativeOracleTests holds renders to the observations: a function
seen to return is not rendered throwing, a wrapper seen to trap is not a
plain return, and the value recovered for six scalar cases, evaluated on
the oracle's inputs, equals what the machine returned (`allows(7, 5)`
through `bics`, `wideCombine(100, 7, 3)` = 79). Reverting each of eight
fixes turns one of them red: E10-b, E10-a, E07-b, the `bics` flags,
F06-a, F05-a, O06-a and E05-a.

**OPEN:** the metatype, cast-target and function-storage fixtures need a
Swift driver (generics and closures) and are not run. Field names are
checked through the value computed from them, not as names.

Hosted CI for `477c832` passed. `cd5db2c` is sprint F06-a.

## 2026-11-23: sprint F06-a, objc_direct inferred from missing metadata

**FIXED (soundness), for authored code.** Twelfth sprint of
[ABI-SPRINTS.md](ABI-SPRINTS.md). A method was taken for `objc_direct`,
with no `_cmd`, when its symbol is `-[C sel]`, C is defined in the image
and the address is in no method list. Absence was the whole of the
evidence. An ordinary IMP that carries a method's symbol name through an
`__asm__` label and is installed with `class_addMethod` has the same
absence and does take `_cmd`:

    long lateImp(id self, SEL _cmd, long a, long b) __asm__("-[Crate late:with:]");

Against `477c832`, the blast radius is one line: the late method's false

## 2026-11-23: sprint F04-a, a virtual tail is not folded through the base body

**GUARDED, not reproduced.** Fifth sprint of
[ABI-SPRINTS.md](ABI-SPRINTS.md). The source read predicted that a tail
call through self's vtable could take the base implementation's
unwritten-result summary and render `return arg0` when an override may
run. It does not. With `class B { func f(_ x: Int) -> Int { x }; func
g(_ x: Int) -> Int { f(x) } }` and an override `f` returning `x &+ 9`,
`B.g` renders `return self.f(arg0)` at -Onone, -O and -Osize, and
`h(x) { f(x) &+ 1 }` renders `return (self.f(arg0) + 1)`.

The mechanism: the dispatch is `ldr x8, [x20]; ldr x1, [x8, #slot]; br
x1`, and the passthrough fold reads only a direct branch's target, so a
branch through a register is never a candidate. `selftail.swift` already
pins self-dispatched tails, so no fixture was added. No code changed.

**OPEN (completeness), seen while probing:** dispatch on an object
argument (`func via(_ b: B, _ x: Int) -> Int { b.f(x) }`) declines as an
unresolved indirect call whose recovered arguments repeat one register
(`[arg1, arg1, …]`), and dispatch on a stored field prints the slot's
method with no receiver (`Virt.Base.pass(arg0)` for `self.b.pass(x)`).
Sprints F01-b and F04-b cover the receiver.

`3625d5b` is sprint E07-b.

## 2026-11-22: local outgoing async descriptor handoff qualification

**Locally qualified at `ff02d78`** on Darwin arm64. The probe records an
outgoing direct handoff when the caller loads the requested context size
from a validated linked descriptor, calls the bound task allocator,
stores the current X22 and return continuation in the new header, and
passes the allocator result in X22 to the descriptor's direct entry.
Incoming owner privacy stays unknown.

The enforcing run passed **2,105 tests / 43 suites (1,443.235 s)**.
The change adds **14 tests** and removes none. All **3,180 cost rows**
met default budgets against the published `3c9b005` baseline. The
**3,176 corpus renders** and four SDK output digests were unchanged.
Postchecks passed **1,110 runs** with identical ordinary output,
including lab text. These comprise 1,092 CLI invocations, eight
serial streaming controls and ten guarded runs across five original
apps. Both binaries produced **84,833 ordered app function headers**.

Eight separate public probe runs used the optimized AwaitResults
fixture. The candidate recorded the same **five outgoing handoffs**
in the JSON array and structured streaming routes, in the same order.
The baseline recorded zero. On each route, exit status and stdout and
stderr bytes agreed across both binaries with recording on or off.
The [probe fields](INSTRUMENTATION.md#scoring-without-parsing-pseudocode) describe machine
provenance for the requested size and continuation.

Incoming ownership, actual allocation extent, runtime write effects and
live scalar transfer remain open.

The original publication gate for `ff02d78` passed **2,105 enforcing
tests / 43 suites (1,423.500 s)** and all **3,180 cost rows** met default
budgets. Total retired instructions increased by **0.04%** and summed
per-run peak footprint decreased by **0.22%**. The gate pushed `ff02d78`
to `dev`. Hosted CI passed **2,105 tests / 43 suites (2,411.742 s)**
on the same published commit.
[Hosted run 45101565065](https://github.com/CamdenBopp/swiftdc/actions/runs/45101565065)

## 2026-11-22: local Go build-ID streaming fix

**Fixed at `9341f33`, published in `3c9b005`** on Darwin arm64. The function
table must identify `go:buildid`, its bytes must carry the Go build-ID
prefix, and the next streaming boundary must agree with the table's
span. The streaming path retains the named empty row, clears the
same-address symbol fold and excludes the data start from executable
call-target analysis. The established array and filtered behavior is
unchanged.

The expanded integration test covers four Go binaries across the
listing, array, filtered and streaming APIs. A new test exercises
exclusion from callable starts. The compiled baseline produced six
issues. Re-enabling only data decoding produced four issues. Re-admitting
only the data start to callable membership produced one. Removing
streaming label normalization failed the pseudocode and structured
output checks. Both CLI commands exited successfully.
The restored focused tests and both label checks passed. The change
expands one test, adds one and removes none.

rules about one register as compact input and expected assembly. Read as
rules and rewritten as hand-made fixtures (clean room: the rules, not the
tests, so nothing is copied), each gives a small checklist swiftdc must
render right.

## Next: native execution as an oracle (2026-11-13)

Prompted by a look at Microlift and Rosemary. The useful part is the
experiment, not either project: compare what swiftdc predicts for a
fixture function with what the CPU does when the function runs on this
Mac. A prototype ran on `libReconstruction.dylib` (`gradeOf`), outside
the tree: an in-process single-step trace through a Mach exception port
needed no entitlement, root or prompt with SIP on, cost 20 to 28 steps
per call, and checked the three branch conditions and the exit x0 over
five inputs (17 verified, 0 refuted; a negated prediction was refuted).
Native first, by priority 5 and 6 above: these give the condition and
return-value fixes independent evidence.

1. **OPEN: check branch decisions against native execution.** Evaluate
   each `values.condition` probe record on chosen inputs and compare it
   with the direction the CPU took in a single-step trace. Denominator:
   every conditional branch in the callable scalar fixtures, with
   never-reached and not-evaluable counted apart, never as passes. Our
   own code only.
2. **OPEN: check register facts at calls and exits against the same
   trace.** Compare `values.call` and `values.exit-registers` (x0, x1,
   x8, x20, x21, d0) with the stepped registers. Denominator: every such
   fact; an unknown is a decline, not a pass.
3. **OPEN: widen the native return oracle past x0.** A thunk that seeds
   x20 and x21 and captures x0, x1, d0 to d3 and x21, so throwing, pair
   and float returns are scored by execution and not from text.
   Denominator: every rendered return value and return outcome in the
   fixtures.
4. **OPEN: a native sample profile mapped to swiftdc's functions.**
   Sampled program counters, unslid by the image's load address and
   bound to it by UUID, bucketed by swiftdc's function ranges and
   cross-checked against `LC_FUNCTION_STARTS`. A sample outside every
   function is a completeness defect; a run with no samples is an error,
   not an empty profile (`sample` returned an empty call graph once).
5. **DEAD END, for now: Microlift as a second oracle.** It is
   GPL-3.0-only, so nothing of it may enter this MIT tree: not vendored,
   no driver that links it, no test that needs it, no committed value
   derived from it. Its AArch64 guest is early by its own README (no
   `bl` in execution, no `br`, `ccmp`, bitfield moves, byte or halfword
   loads, floating point or SIMD) and has no oracle of its own, so a
   disagreement could not be attributed. By mnemonic, the functions it
   could run are ones native execution already covers. Rosemary runs
   apps and observes nothing. Revisit Microlift only as an optional tool
   a developer installs, whose output is compared from outside. If
   symbolic reach is wanted, look at permissively licensed tools first.


## Next: defects from reading the compiler source (2026-11-13)

Thirty agents read the Swift compiler's IRGen, SILGen, stdlib and runtime
sources against swiftdc, one area each. The findings, with the compiler
line that states each rule, are in
[research/compiler-source-read-2026-11-13.md](research/compiler-source-read-2026-11-13.md).
They are leads with a stated reproduction; each becomes FIXED only with
its own fixture and a test seen red. Ordered by the priorities above:
wrong output first, by how much ordinary code it touches.

1. **OPEN: a storage entity's type read as a parameter list.** A setter,
   getter, addressor or key path thunk for a function-typed property is
   seeded from the property's type. FIXED in part: a getter of
   function-typed storage was judged unable to throw, which folded the
   caller's error test to `(0 == 0)`; it may now throw, and the three
   callers in `throwinggetter.swift` keep `error != nil` and decline the
   merged value (60ce7c7). Still open: the entry and call-site seeds, and a
   `@_silgen_name` Swift function, which has no `.` in its name and is
   taken as unable to throw.
2. **FIXED (28df4e7): overflow-guard folding hid preconditions.** A branch
   to a trap on V or carry was dropped without checking which edge
   trapped, which instruction last wrote the flags, or that a carry test
   matched its operation. `precondition(a < b); return a &- b` rendered
   `return (arg0 - arg1)`. The guard now folds only on its arithmetic's
   own overflow; four preconditions in `guardfold.swift` render their
   trap and three real checks still fold. Blast radius is that fixture
   alone, so this is not the mechanism of the open loop bounds-check

3. **FIXED in part (77a2886): stores hidden as runtime noise.** `outlined

4. **FIXED (4eac4f5): a local function's captures.** `$defer` and named

5. **FIXED (c45f1ca): resilient value types.** In a library-evolution image
   a public struct or enum is passed by address and was read from
   registers by field: `afterPoint(_ p: Point, _ n: Int) { n &* 5 }`

7. **FIXED in part (7311942): an outlined fragment's x0/v0** is no longer

9. **OPEN: the declines both rounds ranked first**: globals named by

- **FIXED — an import addend with the top bit set trapped `disasm`,

## Next: features from comparable tools (2026-11-13)

Taken from reads of strongarm (datatheorem), macho_re,
threatflux-binary-analysis, XMachOViewer, retools, HexLab, ktool and jtool;
none of them decompiles Swift. Each fills a gap swiftdc has. Ordered by the
priorities above: completeness and soundness first, reconstruction last.

1. **OPEN: cross-references by selector, string and data symbol.**
   strongarm's `objc_calls_to(classes, selectors)` lists every send of a
   selector, and it cross-references C strings. `xrefs -f` matches only
   function names: `xrefs -f _gCounter` answers "No function matched" for a
   global that exists (second ABI probe, globals). Wanted: `xrefs
   --selector`, `--string` and data-symbol targets, each consulting the
   symbol table before reporting nothing (the empty-result rule), and
   naming defined data symbols in renders, which the probe also found
   missing.
2. **OPEN: block literals.** jtool follows the `str`/`stp` stores that
   build a stack block to name its invoke function and captures. swiftdc
   has no block model (no reference to `_NSConcreteStackBlock` in Sources;
   the first ABI probe: direct block invokes lose returns and captures), so
   every `dispatch_async(queue, ^{…})` and completion handler loses its
   body's link. Wanted: a block literal recognised from a bound isa
   (`_NSConcreteStackBlock`/`GlobalBlock`), an in-image invoke pointer and
   a descriptor, its captures read at their fixed offsets, each part
   declined when not proven.
3. **OPEN: compact unwind as a boundary and frame oracle.** HexLab
   evaluates `__unwind_info`. It describes nearly every function and where
   it saves callee-saved registers: a third boundary source beside
   `LC_FUNCTION_STARTS` and the symbol table (the empty-result rule), and
   the fix for a stripped `bl` target never split when function starts are
   absent (second ABI probe, linker). Its saved-register layout checks the
   frame analysis independently.
4. **OPEN: an A64 semantics coverage audit.** retools generates its
   semantics from the architecture manual. swiftdc models them by hand, and
   gaps are found by luck: `negs` records no flags and `ccmn` declines
   (second ABI probe, integer arithmetic). Wanted: from Arm's
   machine-readable A64 specification, every instruction that writes a
   register or the flags, against what `ValueTracking` models; each
   unmodelled one an OPEN entry, and native execution (as the CCMP tests
   do) the oracle for each one modelled.
5. **OPEN: a built-in resource budget.** threatflux enforces a maximum
   input size and per-parse caps (100,000 records, 4 KiB names, 32 MiB of
   names) with a typed error. swiftdc's preflight declines malformed input,
   but a large app's memory is held only by the external
   `Tools/audit/guard.sh`. Wanted: a footprint budget inside the run that
   fails with a diagnostic naming the limit, never a kill.
6. **OPEN: a reverse-engineering task benchmark.** Sixty practical tasks
   a reverser really does (a type's layout, which function implements a
   requirement, a call's argument values, a branch's condition, an app's
   API endpoints, keychain items, URL routes), each asked of our own
   fixtures and answered by an oracle that is not swiftdc (source,
   `.swiftinterface`, reflection dump, dSYM, native execution). Scored as
   correct, wrong (must stay zero) and declined, per task and optimization
   level, per commit: [research/re-task-benchmark.md](research/re-task-benchmark.md).
   Started from doronz88/swift_reversing's hand-reversing questions. A
   first look: `dump` names no implementation for a resilient
   conformance's requirements.
7. **OPEN: DWARF as a validation oracle.** HexLab imports DWARF. Built
   with `-g`, a fixture's dSYM states its parameters, locals, types and
   field offsets: an independent check of what swiftdc recovers. Today a
   valid dSYM is reported as a malformed Mach-O on every entry point (first
   ABI probe, diagnostics); that is fixed first.
8. **OPEN: a user annotation file.** jtool's companion file holds
   user-edited names and per-argument signatures that later runs read.
   swiftdc's largest error class is a signatureless callee taking stale
   registers as arguments. Wanted: user-stated signatures and names,
   rendered marked as asserted by the user, never as proven.
9. **OPEN: a binary summary.** macho_re and strongarm report signing,
   entitlements, hardened runtime, library validation and the
   `MH_ALLOW_STACK_EXECUTION` and no-heap-execution header flags. swiftdc
   reads `LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO` and reports none of these. Wanted: an `info`
   view of the header flags, the code signature's flags and entitlements,
   and encryption, each read from the binary or reported absent.
10. **OPEN: library signature catalogs.** HexLab matches functions
   against versioned catalogs and reports an ambiguous match as ambiguous.
   For stripped apps with statically linked libraries this names `sub_…`
   functions; a match must be exact and unique, or it declines.
11. **OPEN: control-flow graphs as DOT.** threatflux exports DOT;
   `disasm --cfg` is text only. Wanted: a DOT form of the same graph.
12. **OPEN: cryptographic constants named.** XMachOViewer searches for
   known tables (the AES S-box, SHA and MD5 round constants). A load from
   such a table, matched byte for byte, renders its name instead of a
   `__const` address and an index.

Not taken: patching, `insert_dylib`, re-signing and entitlement injection
(swiftdc reads binaries); entropy and packer heuristics, the ELF, PE, Java
and Wasm formats, kernelcaches and MIG tables (outside the Swift and
Objective-C scope); bitcode extraction (no longer embedded); `.tbd`
generation; a Python API (the JSON output serves scripts); binary diffing
and debugging; an LLM rewrite of the output (it cannot decline, and a
reader cannot tell its guesses from proven facts).

## Assumptions the output depends on

Each render is sound under these ABI facts and no others. Code that breaks
one (hand-written assembly, or Swift that reaches private memory through
unsafe pointers) can be rendered wrongly; each has a fixture that shows the
shape it excludes.

- **The frame record and the prologue's register saves are no object.** A
  pointer to a local below them grants no write to the saved x29 and x30
  (7c04597) or to the x19–x28 the prologue stored before setting x29
  (2026-11-10). The saved x30 coming back intact is already what every
  call's return assumes. A save at or above entry sp is the caller's memory
  and gets no exemption (abi_frame_ownership.s), nor does a body spill after
  the prologue, which may be a word of a local (frame_preserve_alias.s).
  Bytes of the save area the prologue never stored are padding, where LLVM
  places small locals; an address there is a local's and reaches no save.
- **A callee's async context is private to it.** Its caller allocates it but
  keeps no pointer into it, as an argument or anywhere else, so its slots
  change only through the callee's own stores and pointers the callee hands
  out. The original `incomingLeaf` counterexample (async_call_effects.s)
  passes an Int pointing to the callee's slot 16: it rendered `observe(7)`
  against native 11. `774ed5` now retains `observe(?)` instead of that stale
  value (rechecked with this revision's frozen release); general context-slot
  transport and opaque context identities remain open.
- **Unescaped negative save slots are the function's own.** A store through
  an incoming pointer cannot reach them unless the frame's address escaped.
- **Outlined code saves x21 where it writes it.** A chain of fragments
  writing x21 would go unseen by its callers' summaries.
- **A module with no sign of library evolution was built without it.**
  A resilient struct is passed by address, and is recognised only in an
  image that defines an enum-case descriptor, a dispatch thunk or a
  stored-property descriptor (`LibraryEvolutionEvidence`). A resilient
  module whose public types have no public stored property, enum, class
  or protocol defines none of them, and its public structs would be read
  from registers by field. No fixture shows it: such a module's symbols
  and sections equal a plain build's, so there is nothing to detect.

## 1. Soundness — can it fabricate or misattribute semantics?

- **FIXED — a callee could reuse the stack below the caller's sp.** A
  frame fact below the call-time sp, or any frame fact once sp is unknown
  after a dynamically sized stack adjustment, survived an unproved call,
  though the callee may allocate or reuse that storage: stack_lifetime.s
  returns 99 natively where swiftdc read the earlier callee's 7, and
  `sub sp, sp, x20` with an unproven size may move sp up over a live slot.
  Such facts are now forgotten at an unproved call (the tracer and the
  preservation summary share `FrameMemoryEffect.calleeStack`). Ported from
  the compiler-ir-integration-20261106 worktree. Cost: GoodLinks
  unresolved indirect calls 12,577 -> 15,531, nearly all in functions
  whose sp is unknown (generic code sizing a buffer from a type's runtime
  size); the exact-sp rule alone costs none.

- **FIXED — a `___chkstk_darwin`-proven allocation forgot the whole
  frame.** Swift sizes a stack buffer from a type's runtime size and
  probes it first; the probe faults unless `sp - x9` is a valid downward
  allocation. sp moving from an exact frame offset k (or from a proven
  allocation below it) by the probed x9, or its 16-byte rounding, now
  keeps facts at and above k across an unproved call. A memory write or
  another call between probe and allocation ends the proof, since a
  reload of the size can then read a different value; an unprobed
  adjustment anywhere in the chain still forgets everything.
  stack_lifetime.s carries native counterexamples for each. GoodLinks
  unresolved indirect calls 15,531 -> 14,853 (`swiftdc xrefs GoodLinks
  --unreferenced --probe - --probe-filter
  event=cfg.unresolved-indirect-call`); countAll's associated-type
  witness names are back.
- **FIXED — a call through a pure branch thunk lost its inputs.** A body
  that is one direct `b` to another declared function (a merged witness, an
  outlined relay) proved no input of its own, so its callers rendered
  `sub_ad0()` or `witness(?, ?, ?)` where the target reads x0. Register
  summaries now carry the target's proved integer and floating-point inputs,
  with their widths, backwards through such an alias. Both the alias's and
  the target's decoded entry must match their summary keys; a body with a
  prologue, a move, a call, an indirect or conditional branch, a cycle or a
  missing target gains nothing. PureTailInputTests covers every summary
  route. Ported from the compiler-ir-arc-origin-20261107 worktree.

- **FIXED (soundness, 2026-11-10) — an entry spill was used as an escaped
  local's object bound; ported with the rest of the frame-ownership work.**
  `frame_preserve_alias.s`: an x19 spill that is a word of the local passed
  to a call was kept across it, where native execution rewrites it. An
  escaped local's MAY reach is now its whole frame. Ported from the
  compiler-ir-frame-ownership worktree (Codex) together with its entry-register
  roles, indirect-result and context-result producer order, complete-body
  register transfer, caller-owned frame aliases and imported-receiver proofs.
- **DECIDED and FIXED (2026-11-10, completeness): an escaped local's
  address no longer reaches its frame's record.** The cost above came from
  `otherWide`-like bodies: a local passed to a callee with no store plan
  could reach the whole frame, the saved x29 included, so the body was
  summarised as clobbering x29 and 47ceb26 escaped every caller's frame.
  The policy: the frame record (the entry x29 and x30 the prologue stores at
  the frame pointer) is no object of the frame, so a pointer to a local below
  it grants no write there. The analysis already assumes the saved x30 comes
  back intact at every call; the x29 beside it is the same assumption. The
  exemption holds only while nothing that could address the record has
  escaped: the frame pointer itself, an address at or above it, an address
  that escaped before the record was written, a frame address spilled below
  sp, a callee that reads x29, or an unmodelled store of a frame alias each
  keep the record reachable (`recordReachable`, joined by OR). The register
  saves between the locals and the record get no exemption. Against
  9369b0e: 33 fixtures, 4,779 structured lines, `?`-bearing lines 768 ->
  263 (whole results bound and returned, call arguments named, spills read
  back); GoodLinks cfg.unresolved-indirect-call 15,504 -> 15,350.
  `frame_preserve_alias.s`, the soundness counterexample, still renders
  `return ?`. Bounded writes through passed pointers (a callee's own store
  extents) remain the precise fix for the saves below the record.
- **OPEN — unknown-sp sites remain (audited 2026-11-10).** The 2,276 figure
  (14,853 − 12,577) is stale: GoodLinks has 15,504 unresolved indirect calls
  at 9369b0e, and the unknown-sp share is not separated from the
  frame-ownership cost. Stripped countAll (libAssociatedWitness.stripped
  `sub_590`) names its witnesses since the argument-metadata size is followed
  (2026-11-10). The preservation
  summary forgot every saved value when sp was not exact; since 774a43e it
  keeps a `___chkstk_darwin`-probed allocation's bound, as the tracer does.
  Re-measured 2026-11-11 at d49207f: GoodLinks has 10,849 unresolved
  indirect calls. Since 2ec4e99 (12,451) the probe proof survives pushes and
  pops of stack arguments (e978917, 5581ef5, 32bfbfe, d49207f), spills of
  the new sp (d1754ef), long chains (d997846), sizes only the summary

  holding a frame address in 9 (d674f17 removed those it never reads), and
  an unbounded value in 4.

- **FIXED — a callee that may clobber x29 left the caller's frame
  intact.** A call to a body summarised as not preserving x29, made while
  x29 held a frame address, forgot only the register. The callee can
  keep that address, reload it, or hand it to a later callee that writes

- **FIXED — a generic function's metadata was counted past an argument

- **FIXED — a global variable's addressor took x20 and the argument

  not prove it: the toolchain's `libSwiftOperators` keeps `standardOperators`,

- **FIXED — a float's bit pattern rendered as the float, and integer
  constants beside it as float literals.** `fmov x8, d0` carried the
- **FIXED (3e1b1df) — a float's bit pattern rendered as the float, and
  integer constants beside it as float literals.** `fmov x8, d0` carried the
  Double into the general register unchanged, so every integer operation
  on its bits read as one on the Double and `floatWidth` typed the
  constants as Doubles. Swift -O `Int(a)` guards finiteness with `fmov x8,
  d0; and x8, x8, #0x7fffffffffffffff; cmp x8, x9; b.gt trap`, which read
  `(arg0 & 0x7fffffffffffffff) > 1.7976931348623157e+308`: a float compare
  that is false on NaN, where the binary traps. `a.bitPattern ==
  0x7ff8000000000001` read `arg0 != nan`, always true as written. The
  move now writes `.unary(.bitPattern(bits:), v)`, rendered `v.bitPattern`
  for a proven float of that width, `?` for a float of another width
  (`fmov x0, d0` over a Float argument read `return arg0`), and `v` for a
  value not known to be a float. It types as an integer of unknown sign,
  so each compare keeps its machine signedness (`<=ᵁ`). `fmov dN, xM` of a
  bit pattern is the float again. Fixtures `floatbits.swift` (-O and
  -Onone) and `floatbitswidth.s`; blast radius 6 files, 36 structured
  lines, all `fmov xN, dM` sites, swift-syntax byte-identical.
- **FIXED (c146d65) — a constant beside a bit-level operator over a
  float read as a float.** `floatWidth` recursed through every binary operator, so `(x &
  mask) cmp imm` over a float argument typed `imm` as a Double; the
  float-literal rule skipped only an outer bit-level operator. A bit-level
  binary (`& | ^ << >> >>ᵁ`) and an integer-only unary (`~`, byte swap,
  leading zeros or sign bits, bit reverse) now end the float context. It
  covers routes with no `fmov`: -Onone `unsafeBitCast(a, to: Int.self)`
  spills d0 and reloads it, and `& 0xff == 7` read `((arg0 & 255) !=

- **FIXED (07db3fe) — the reverse move, `fmov dN, xM` of an integer,
  carried the integer bare.** `Double(bitPattern: i) * 2.0` at -O is `fmov d0, x0;

- **FIXED — a nested call drops `Double.init(bitPattern:)`'s label.** -Onone
  calls the initializer, and as an argument it rendered

  one whose parameters are all `_` keeps the bare name. Labels go on the

- **FIXED (`4266f7c`) — a float spilled and reloaded into a general register carries

- **FIXED — a word spilled from one register file and reloaded into the
  other carried its value bare.** -Onone `unsafeBitCast(a, to: Int.self)`
- **FIXED (4266f7c) — a word spilled from one register file and reloaded
  into the other carried its value bare.** -Onone `unsafeBitCast(a, to: Int.self)`
  is `str d0, [sp]; ldr x9, [sp]`, with no `fmov`, and `~bits == 7`,
  lowered to `0 - x - 1`, rendered `((-arg0 - 5e-324) != 3.5e-323)`. The
  other way, `str x0, [sp]; ldr d0, [sp]` rendered the Int as the Double.
  A frame word now records the register file that stored it
  (`Location.stackFile`), and a reload into the other file is
  `.bitPattern` or `.floatFromBits`: `((-arg0.bitPattern - 1) != 7)`,
  `(Double(bitPattern: arg0) + 1.0)`. A float register reading a word of
  another width declines, as does one reading part of a general store. A
  `q` load is left alone, and a word with no known file (an entry
  argument, a `memcpy`, an indirect result) claims nothing; paths that
  disagree on a word's file lose the word. A self field declared as that
  float stays the field: -Onone copies `self.radius` through x8. The
  bit-level stop above is
  what still types a `memcpy`'d word's constants (`floatbitswidth.s`).

- **FIXED — a setter dispatch folded into an assignment of x0 whatever
  the property's type.** A vtable call to self's own setter renders as

  `label = ""` read `self.label = 0`. A Double travels in d0, so `scale =
  0.5` read `self.scale = <the setter's own address>`. The value is now
  the parameter as its type travels: one integer register, one float
  register (a constant at the type's width), or a String's two words as a
  literal, a String call result or a String field. Anything else is not
  folded. Fixture `setterfold.swift`.

- **FIXED — a value-witness call took the registers around it as

  getEnumTagSinglePayload 3, storeEnumTagSinglePayload 4, getEnumTag 2,

- **FIXED — `CalleeRegisterSummary.readsSelfRegister` was wrong
  both ways.** Its forward pass tracked writes to x0-x7, x29 and x22, but
  not x20, so a body that overwrites x20 before using it counted as
  reading its caller's x20, and the caller showed a `self:` that is no
  argument. Tracking x20 as a write was not enough: `uses` ignored any
  store of x20 to an sp-based slot as a register save, and -Onone spills
  the incoming `self` that way (`Reconstruction.Dog.init`: `str x20,
  [sp, #8]; ldr x20, [sp, #8]; bl Animal.init`). A spilled `self`
  reloaded into another register was missed outright. Now
  `Preservation.selfRegisterFlow` is a may-analysis of where the incoming
  x20 lives: registers through 64-bit moves, frame slots (offsets from
  entry sp, via `Preservation`'s sp/x29 tracking) through spills and
  reloads, unions at joins. Any other use, a store it cannot place, a
  call input, a `ret` with it in x0-x7 (`Animal.init` returns its self),
  an unplaceable load or a call while an escaped frame address may reach
  a slot holding it, is a read. Blast radius (`Tools/blast-radius.sh
  --real`): structured 6 files, 104 lines; 18 `self:` arguments dropped
  from in-image callees that load x20 before using it (`Tree.sum` on a
  by-value enum, `childNameForDiagnostics`, `resolveLexicalContext`,
  specializations of `Sequence.contains`, `_copySequenceContents`,
  `_copySequenceToContiguousArray` and the allocating and region-visitor
  inits), each checked against its body; `Dog.init(self:
  swift_allocObject(…))` and `Animal.init(self: …)` keep it.
